evals.name: review-ai-generated-banking-screen
evals.prompt:
An AI tool generated this mobile banking home screen. Review it and tell me what to fix.

- Purple top bar with the logo, a pink notification dot, and a bright purple avatar circle
- Balance card: 'Balance' label in 16px bold, '$2,340.18' in 16px bold, 'Updated 2 min ago' in 16px bold, all centre-aligned
- Four action tiles in coloured boxes: Send (green), Request (orange), Top up (blue), More (red)
- Bottom tab bar: Home, Cards, a large purple '+' button in the middle, Activity, Profile
- Settings form: a dropdown 'Statement frequency' with options Weekly / Monthly / Quarterly
- Logout dialog: title 'Are you sure?', buttons 'YES' and 'NO'
evals.expected_output: A findings list keyed to rule IDs, most severe first: the action in the tab bar, the dropdown for three options, the 'Are you sure?' dialog, flat hierarchy in the balance card, centre-aligned multi-line text, and excess colour in the chrome and tiles, each with a concrete fix.

assertions.text: flags the '+' button inside the tab bar and says tab bars are for navigation only (CMP-1)
recommends radio buttons (or a segmented control) instead of the dropdown for 3 options (CMP-2)
rewrites the dialog with a verb + noun title such as 'Log out?' and action-labelled buttons such as 'Cancel' / 'Log out' (CMP-3, CMP-8)
makes the balance amount the hero element, larger than its label and timestamp (HIE-1 or HIE-2)
calls out the multi-colour chrome or tiles and recommends neutral chrome with one primary colour (VIS-6)
uses the RULE-ID: problem → fix format
does not list rules that pass

evals.name: build-delete-dialog-react
evals.prompt: Write a React + Tailwind confirmation dialog for deleting a project. The project name is passed in as a prop.
evals.expected_output: A dialog component whose title is a verb + noun, whose body names the project and states the consequence, with Cancel and a destructive 'Delete project' button, left-aligned, with a close control.

assertions.text: title is a verb + noun question such as 'Delete project?', not 'Are you sure?'
body interpolates the project name prop and states the action can't be undone
buttons are labelled 'Cancel' and 'Delete project' (or 'Delete'), never Yes/No/OK
destructive button uses a danger colour and sits on the trailing side after Cancel
includes a dismiss (×) control in the header
text is left-aligned, not text-center
button labels are not uppercase

evals.name: dark-mode-token-setup
evals.prompt: Set up the colour tokens for our app as CSS custom properties with light and dark themes. Today the components use hex values directly: #FFFFFF, #F7F7F7, #EDEFF3, #777F8A, #191B1F for greys and #E8EFFD, #2966E9 for blue.
evals.expected_output: A primitive layer (grey-100…grey-500, blue-100/blue-…) holding the hex values, and a semantic layer named by element/priority/state that aliases primitives differently per theme, with dark surfaces getting lighter as they elevate.

assertions.text: defines primitive tokens named family-weight (e.g. --grey-100, --blue-500) holding the raw hex values
defines semantic tokens following color-{element}-{priority}-{state}, e.g. --color-bg, --color-bg-surface, --color-text-primary
semantic tokens reference primitives via var(), not raw hex
light and dark themes change only the semantic layer's aliases; primitives are not redefined per theme
in dark mode, elevated surfaces are lighter shades of dark, and no surface token maps to a light grey or white
states that components should reference semantic tokens only

evals.name: nested-radius-card
evals.prompt: I have a product card with 8px padding and an image inside it with a 12px corner radius. The card itself has a 12px radius too and the corners look off. What radius should the card be? Give me the CSS.
evals.expected_output: The card radius should be 20px (inner 12 + padding 8), expressed as a calc() or fixed value.

assertions.text: answers 20px for the outer card radius
states the rule outer = inner + padding
CSS sets the card border-radius to 20px or calc(12px + 8px) / calc(var(--inner) + var(--pad))

evals.name: signup-header-buttons
evals.prompt: Our marketing site header has two black buttons on the right: 'Sign in' and 'Sign up'. We have a free plan. Improve the buttons.
evals.expected_output: Sign in becomes a ghost button for returning users, the sign-up button stays primary, and its label becomes verb + product + value (e.g. 'Get <Product> free').

assertions.text: makes 'Sign in' a ghost or text button and keeps one primary button (CMP-6)
rewrites the sign-up label as verb + product + value, e.g. 'Get Acme free' (CMP-8)
does not leave two primary buttons
